messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: autopager fired -> service=inference-gateway, region=us-west1, symptom=5xx_rate_spike, rate=4.7% (baseline 0.2%)

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty incident PD-84211 created and auto-notified rotation. Unacked: 2. Escalation policy: infra-oncall -> runtime-team.

ben_oncall: ack. I'm on it — collecting quick signal. Can someone check k8s pod status for inference-gateway in us-west1?

charlie_infra: running quick check: `kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=inference-gateway -o wide` shows 3/5 pods ready on us-west1-a, two pods in CrashLoopBackOff on node gw-5.

dave_sre: grabbing logs from the crashing pods: `kubectl -n inference logs inference-gateway-7f4d -c gateway` -> seeing repeated `ERR: kvcache: failed to connect to redis backend` + connection reset errors to edge-proxy. Might be kv-cache flapping.

emily_support: FYI support telemetry: 4 paying customers reported 502s in last 10m (Acme, BetaCorp, NimbusAI, Luma). Severity P2 customer impact being tracked.

ben_oncall: ok. Immediate mitigation plan: 1) remove unhealthy pods from LB, 2) fail traffic to secondary region (us-east1) via traffic-shepherding policy, 3) restart kv-cache sidecars, 4) escalate to infra runtime if redis unreachable. Doing step 1 now.

charlie_infra: removed pods inference-gateway-7f4d and inference-gateway-9a3b from service endpoints. LB marked them draining. Applying canary swap to send 30% to us-east1: `infractl route update --service inference-gateway --region-split us-west1=70,us-east1=30 --reason "5xx spike"`

pagerduty-bot: PD-84211 acknowledged by ben_oncall. Escalation to runtime-team requested.

ben_oncall: restart sidecars on the two nodes that reported redis errors: `kubectl -n infra rollout restart daemonset/kv-cache-sidecar --selector node=gw-5` — doing now.

dave_sre: sidecar restart succeeded on gw-5. I'm seeing drop in connection resets in logs. 5xx rate dropping from 4.7% -> 1.1% over 3m. Still above baseline.

emily_support: customers Acme and BetaCorp on standby for status updates. They're asking for ETA. Recommending a proactive note: "we're mitigating a transient error condition; routing to secondary region; engineers are investigating; next update in 20m"

ben_oncall: agreed. Posting status to customers and support. Also tagging postmortem owner: charlie_infra.

charlie_infra: investigating root cause: redis cluster in us-west1 reported increased failover latency at 06:12Z -> a subset of gateway pods attempted to reconnect repeatedly and hit transient errors causing 502s. Filing to follow-up with infra-db team.

dave_sre: mitigation complete for now: canary split stable at 80/20 us-west1/us-east1, 5xx rate holding at 0.26% current. Rolling restart scheduled for remaining gateway pods in us-west1 over next 15m to ensure healthy reconnections.

ben_oncall: handing off to night-shift at 07:00Z. Handoff notes: PD-84211, root suspected: redis failover flapping, mitigations applied: pod removal, sidecar restart, traffic split to us-east1, rolling restarts. If 5xx climbs >1% re-escalate to infra-db.

emily_support: copying handoff to support: ticket created TKT-5543 linking PD-84211 and customer impact list.

incident-bot: incident closed (auto) after 30m without new pages. PD-84211 status -> resolved (root cause investigation pending).

charlie_infra: postmortem owner assigned. Will include timeline, redis metrics, and suggestions: stricter redis failover backoff, sidecar backpressure handling, and an automated preemptive traffic-shepherd when redis M+1 failovers detected.

ben_oncall: thanks team. Quick retro: add a short runbook snippet to inference-gateway runbook for "redis failover -> traffic-shepherding". I'll put a PR.
